doc.title: Jerome Richardson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

title: Preferred instruments and plans for a new record
summary: He favors soprano sax, is practicing flute and piccolo, and names players and repertoire for his upcoming record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well do you have an instrument that you like to play the most these days?
You ever get your piccolo out anymore?

Oh, I have to practice. Practice, practice. Last night I took out my flutes. The day before I was playing a little piccolo just to keep my chopping okay. But I want to, I’ve been practicing a lot of saxophone because I haven’t been asked to play flute too much lately, but I also know that I’ve got to get my flute back together like I should. Because on this record I might play some flute, or I’m looking to do some flute playing. I’ve got some original pieces and I want to do a thing with Villa Lobos, the Bachianas #5, and a couple of things. So I’ve really got to get my chops together.
Who do you hope to use on this upcoming record?

Lewis Nash, Russell — what’s his name — Monroe, plays guitar. And who else? The bass player — oh, I don’t know. We haven’t decided on a bass player yet because it was George Mraz and I heard George Mraz had some difficulty about the date. It might be Peter Washington, who is very fine. And we haven’t settled it yet.

Well I look forward to it. I hope it goes well for you. Is there any dates, you know, I don’t know if the students have any idea what it might be like to get a call to do a session, © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-
